description: One security finding. Deliberately polymorphic — the detectors differ, but triage, acknowledgement and routing are the same for all of them.

fields.label: Severity
fields.description: Critical is out-of-band and immediate. High is an hourly digest, Medium a daily one, Info dashboard only. The tier decides routing, so it is set by the detector and never by hand.

fields.label: Category
fields.description: Which detector raised it — persistence, accounts, network, filesystem. Used for grouping and for suppression scoped to one detector.

fields.label: Subject
fields.description: One line, and the deduplication key together with the date. Must identify the CONDITION, not the measurement — a value that drifts makes every reading a new alert.

fields.label: Suppressed Until
fields.description: Silence expires on its own. Permanent suppression is how alerting dies, so there is no way to set one.

fields.label: What To Do
fields.description: What it means, what to check, and what a false positive looks like. With one operator, an alert whose response has to be reconstructed from memory each time gets ignored within a month.

fields.label: Dedupe Key
fields.description: Subject plus the day. Two events with the same key are the same condition reported twice, and only the first is kept.

fields.label: Occurrences
fields.description: How many times this condition was seen while the alert stood open. Counted rather than duplicated.

name: Security Event
